# PARSE001: malformed-directive

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| family | PARSE |
| product | frob |
| severity (default) | error |
| tier | universal |
| scope | file |
| fix | manual |
| polarity | P+ |
| must_measure | false |
| version | 1 |
| since | 2.0.0 |

A `frob:` directive is malformed: unterminated quote, bad key, missing or invalid argument.

The scanner never silently drops a directive line it recognises by
namespace; if the arguments cannot be read into the verb's declared shape
the finding points at the exact offending token. Fix the directive text
so it matches `<namespace>:<verb> <args>` with `key=value` or
`key="quoted value"` pairs.

## Examples

### PARSE001 malformed directive / Rust: unterminated quote #1 (line 6) (fire)

```rust
/* frob:accept COV006 because="oops */ // error: PARSE001
fn a() {}
```

### PARSE001 malformed directive / Rust: missing required argument #2 (line 13) (fire)

```rust
/* frob:accept COV006 */ // error: PARSE001
fn a() {}
```
